Subject: Production errors & latency spike - Quantisys inference

Naomi / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx responses and tail latency for our LLM-backed checkout validation flow beginning ~07:45 PST. Error rate jumped to ~7% and p95 latency is ~1.8s (baseline 220ms). This is affecting ~15% of user requests and causing failed payment validations. Our dashboard shows reserved capacity throttles around the dedicated GPU pool assigned to our account; we have a monthly reserved commit.

Can someone confirm whether this is capacity saturation on your side or a model/regression on our prompts? We need an urgent mitigation plan — can you open a bridge and advise temporary fallbacks?

- Oliver

- Marissa, can ops validate whether the dedicated pool for Quantisys is saturated (GPU util / queue length) and if any backpressure/fallbacks triggered?

On Mon, 2027-05-04 at 08:26, naomi.feldman@redwood.ai wrote:
> Naomi — thanks for the report and the timestamps, appreciated. We're opening an ops bridge now and pulling telemetry.

Update from ops/serving: we see sustained queue growth on pool gpu-dedicated-east-14 that hosts Quantisys' reserved shards. Key points:
- GPU util at 98% on several shards, queue depth rising from ~10k to ~45k requests in the 07:30-08:50 window.
- KV cache miss rate spiked (per-route) after a large batch of new user profiles started hitting the system — cache warming stalled and mem pressure forced repeated recompute.
- Error bursts are correlated with token timeouts (5xx) when requests exceed per-shard queue thresholds; p95 jump matches customer's telemetry.

Proposed immediate actions (can do within 10–20m):
1) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for the checkout route (we have a cached snapshot) — reduces repeated compute.
2) Promote a smaller quantized model (gpt-sm-qdq) for low-latency callers and route high-QPS traffic there.
3) Apply short-term traffic shaping: split 20% of traffic to hosted fallback.

I attached a quick metrics dump for your visibility (pool-metrics-20270504.csv) and a KV cache dump (kv-cache-dump-20270504.txt).

Aditya — we need temporary burst: +4 shards for 90 minutes to drain queue if execs approve.

—Marissa

Subject: Resolution & next steps — Quantisys incident (08:12 PST)

Oliver — final update from today's bridge and remediation steps completed: 

What happened:
- Dedicated GPU shard pool experienced saturation due to a traffic pattern change that caused a KV cache miss storm. That increased compute and queue depth, leading to token timeouts and higher 5xx.

What we did (completed by 12:15 PST):
1) Enabled aggressive KV/prefix caching for the checkout route — reduced recompute by ~60%.
2) Rolled 20% of incoming QPS to a hosted, quantized fallback model (gpt-sm-qdq) for the highest-QPS callers.
3) Infra applied a temporary +4 shard burst for 90 minutes to drain queues and restore headroom.
4) Ops validated tail latency/p95 returned to baseline within ~30m of mitigations.

Compensation & next steps:
- Sales proposed a one-time credit to Quantisys; David is coordinating.
- We're scheduling a follow-up technical review (deep-dive) with your infra team tomorrow 10:00 PST to go over cache tuning and a permanent mitigation (reserved headroom guardrails, autoscaling thresholds, and per-route static fallbacks).
- We'll provide the full incident packet (metrics, logs, runbook changes) by EOD.

Please reply with a quick confirmation if Latency and error rates look stable on your side and if you accept the proposed follow-up time.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll take ownership on the post-mortem and make the recommended platform changes.

—Naomi
